decision: Accept the exact dated articles for local source integration; production acceptance remains pending

records.determination: One Mombasa–Nairobi Phase 1 railway with passenger and freight roles. Later extensions and receiving facilities remain separate. Inaugural vehicle movement, capacity, targets and cumulative service totals do not become a recurring Phase 1 performance or financial finding.

One Nairobi City County, not metropolitan catchment or a sum of neighbourhood facilities. Framework approval, reported service milestones and expansion plans retain their own stages and dates; no causal education or employment result is admitted.

One Mombasa County with island and mainland areas, not the entire corridor or trading catchment. Two station percentages remain separate and their forecast is not an opening. A historical interruption duration is not observed restoration or current water supply.

review_checks: Fifteen selected sources inspected November 22 in America/Edmonton: fourteen official English HTML bodies and selected administrative prose from the county's English development-plan PDF. Author self-review is not independent acceptance.

The PDF cover and complete text of printed pages 1 and 4 were read. Web screenshot calls returned no visible image; an attempted local download was denied by network permissions. No visual-rendering claim, statistical-table analysis, bypass or dependency installation is made.

Nairobi's about and 2026 mobility-agenda pages, Nairobi Water FAQ and supply-day pages, and Mombasa's climate-department page timed out. An earlier Mombasa commuter-project page failed retrieval. Those candidate pages are excluded, not treated as inspected bodies or evidence of nonexistence.

MOWASSCO's November 16, 2026 notice listing was visible on its homepage, but the exact notice route exposed only navigation to the text reader. No content or restoration finding is borrowed from the separate March 18, 2025 notice. The November listing is not one of the fifteen selected article sources.

All three named identities were screened against the historical eligibility, Phase 119, Phase 191/192 and current additive named accounts. They are new identities with no reused country acquisition docket.

Three articles contain eighteen substantive sections and thirteen chronology events. Each has five source-bound sections and an editorial next-evidence section. Mombasa's chronology also cites the shared SGR opening source.

The Mombasa–Nairobi line is one Phase 1 project. Passenger inauguration and commercial freight start use different dates; the later extension, transit shed and feeder stations are dependencies rather than new project admissions.

Published service patterns are not observed runs or punctuality. The service page's questionable night-service clock entry is not reproduced, and booking, tariffs and live availability were not tested.

October 29 vehicle movement is distinct from its November 2 publication and the target of 700 vehicles per month. Up to 1,000 TEU at the transit shed is capacity, not measured throughput. Cumulative anniversary statistics do not become a Phase 1-only annual series or unique-person count.

Nairobi's county profile supports identity and broad institutional year only. Its linked third-party material, undated area and population statistics are not reused. The metropolitan transit framework is not an operating railway or achieved emissions/travel-time effect.

September 4 neighbourhood and school-meal publications are not exact facility-opening dates. Fifty million meals are repeated service units, not unique children. Continued works at other neighbourhood sites remain distinct from the named reported facilities.
The October 27 Jericho account reports an already-launched hub but supplies no exact opening day. A plan for all 85 wards is not 85 completed hubs or demonstrated employment gains.

Mombasa's 2023–2027 planning period is not an inferred adoption/publication date. Printed administrative prose supplies the six-sub-county scope; no area, census projection, port-throughput or map measurement is imported.

Changamwe East's 52 percent and West's 38 percent are independent October construction figures. End-November completion remains a forecast. The March 2025 water notice's approximate 72 hours is a promised interruption duration, not actual restoration.

Earlier portfolio decisions, every preceding cohort, all 34 translated readings and evidence-cycle identities remain intact. Local source integration does not authorize production cleanup, full acceptance, publication, launch or elapsed stewardship.
